about.visionText: Founded in the heart of New York, Start Door To Door is a customer focused courier company dedicated to reliability and speed. We connect businesses and individuals with a seamless door to door delivery experience, powered by advanced routing, safety protocols, and real-time visibility.
about.teamText: We believe in transparency, fair pricing, and unmatched service. Our local team knows NYC streets and delivers with a mission to exceed expectations on every delivery.
about.p1Copy: If a window is tight or a route is busy, you hear it before you book, not after the parcel is late.
about.p2Copy: You reach a person who can see the job and make a decision, not a queue that reads from a script.
about.p3Copy: Fragile handling, correct vehicle, and proof of delivery on every job — not an upsell.

sending.title: What we carry, and what we can't
sending.cant5: Cash, and perishables that can't survive the trip
sending.note: Restrictions on dangerous goods come from federal transport rules, not just from us. If you're unsure about an item, ask before you book.
sending.pack1: Use a rigid box with room for cushioning on every side.
sending.pack2: Wrap fragile contents individually and fill the gaps so nothing shifts.
sending.pack3: Seal every seam with tape, then mark the box FRAGILE or THIS WAY UP.
sending.pack4: Put the full delivery address and a phone number on the outside.

q1.a: Same-day jobs move within hours of pickup rather than on a fixed timetable — the exact window depends on distance, traffic, and when the parcel is ready. We confirm a realistic window when you book, and the tracking page shows the current status.

q2.q: How do I track my parcel?
q2.a: Every parcel is scanned at each handover. Enter your tracking number on the tracking page to see the latest scan, the current milestone, and the estimated arrival when one is available.

q3.q: What happens if nobody is there to receive it?
q3.a: The courier contacts the number on the job. Depending on what you've asked for, we can leave it with a neighbour, return it to the depot for a second attempt, or hold it for collection. Nothing is left unattended without your instruction.

q4.q: Do you provide proof of delivery?
q4.a: Yes. Deliveries are closed with a signature or a delivery note recording who took the parcel, and the date and time. It appears on your tracking timeline.

q5.q: How is the price worked out?
q5.a: Price depends on distance, parcel size and weight, how quickly it has to move, and whether it needs two people or inside delivery. Send us the details and you get a quote before anything is booked.

q6.q: Can you handle regular, repeating deliveries?
q6.a: Yes. Recurring pickups and scheduled routes are set up for business accounts — same driver window, same route, on the days you choose.

handling.title: The care rules we work to

h1.title: Scanned at every handover
h1.copy: Pickup, sorting, transit, and delivery each produce a scan, so there is a record of where the parcel has been.

h2.title: Chain of custody on request
h2.copy: For medical, legal, and sensitive items we can record who held the parcel at each step and hand it over person to person.

h3.title: The right vehicle for the load
h3.copy: Bikes for documents through the traffic, cars for parcels, vans for furniture and bulk. The load decides, not the schedule.

h4.title: Closed with proof
h4.copy: A signature or delivery note with a time stamp closes the job, and stays on the shipment timeline.

trackingHelp.s2: At sorting — it has been scanned at a hub and routed onward.
trackingHelp.s3: In transit — it is moving between hubs or towards the delivery area.
trackingHelp.s4: Out for delivery — it is loaded for the final run today.
trackingHelp.s5: Delivered — handed over, with a signature or delivery note.
trackingHelp.s6: Needs attention — something is blocking delivery; contact support and we'll sort it.
trackingHelp.help1: A new number can take a little while to appear — scans start at the first pickup.
trackingHelp.help2: Check the number against the confirmation you were sent; letters and digits are easy to mix up.
trackingHelp.help3: Still nothing? Send us the number and the pickup address and we'll trace it.

galleryPage.title: A day on the route
galleryPage.intro: Nine moments from the work itself — packing, pickup, the hub, the road, and the handover at the door.

i1.title: Marked before it moves
i1.caption: Fragile contents get written on the box, not just noted on the docket. The handler who picks it up can see it.

i2.title: Bike courier, city centre
i2.caption: Documents and small parcels move faster on two wheels when traffic is standing still.

i3.title: Loading at the kerb
i3.caption: Boxes stacked heaviest first, then walked to the van — no dragging, no dropping.

i4.title: Manifest before departure
i4.caption: Every parcel on board is checked against the run sheet before the doors close.

i5.title: Pallet handling
i5.caption: Bulk and heavy freight moves on a forklift at the hub, away from the parcel line.

i6.title: Scanned into the network
i6.caption: Each scan is what puts a new line on your tracking page — pickup, hub, transit, delivery.

i7.title: Route sheet, last check
i7.caption: Drop order set, addresses confirmed, and the tight windows flagged before the run starts.

i8.title: Residential drop
i8.caption: Van at the kerb, parcels carried to the door — the part of the job the customer actually sees.

i9.title: Large item, hand carried
i9.caption: Bulky items go from van to doorstep by hand, and inside if that is what was booked.
